statement: Typing into the search box does nothing; the order list never filters.
Searching by customer name matches nothing because the filter checks the item field instead.
The deployed site always shows one fake "Test User" order no matter what's in the real order data.

category: works in dev but not on the production build
statement: The deployed page never loads its script; the build forgot to copy app.js into the output, so the browser gets a 404 and the search box stays disabled forever.
The total shown on the page undercounts because it leaves out the last order in the filtered list.
Orders on the page are sorted by price, most expensive first, instead of appearing in their original order.
The "Loading orders" message never goes away, even after the orders have loaded and search is enabled.
Loading the site's homepage returns 404 Not Found because the server looks for home.html instead of index.html.
Requesting any file that doesn't exist crashes the server with an unhandled exception instead of returning 404.
If PORT isn't set, the server doesn't fail clearly; it silently starts listening on a random port that nothing can find.
Every order on the page shows the item name "Widget", no matter what was actually ordered.
Running the production build fails outright with a module-not-found error, so there is nothing to deploy.

category: works in dev but not on the production build
statement: The built site's data file is named orders-data.json but the page still requests /orders.json, so the order list never loads (404) after a production build, even though the same files work if served ad hoc in a dev sandbox.
The search box never becomes usable; it stays greyed out even after orders finish loading.
Typing a search still shows the total for every order, not just the ones matching the search.
The page never runs its script because the tag points at /main.js, a file the server never serves.
Searching for a customer with no orders crashes the page's script instead of showing a $0 total.
The order list shows results in reverse order compared to the underlying data.
Package installs no longer link the web app's workspace at all, so the build can't find its own app directory.
Running the deploy's build script fails immediately: it looks for build.js, but the real script is build.mjs.
Each row on the page shows the item name before the customer's name, reversed from what the page is supposed to show.
The total on the page shows a garbled number like "0480095" instead of the correct sum, because of a string-concatenation bug.
The server stops declaring a content type for the orders data file, serving it as application/octet-stream instead of application/json.
Searching for a customer's last name (like "Nguyen") finds nothing; only matches at the very start of the name work now.
The build fails outright: the shared orders module has invalid syntax, so nothing can be built or served.
The orders page never finishes loading; it fetches a data file that doesn't exist, and there is no error message, just the loading spinner forever.

category: works in dev but not on the production build
statement: Every price on the deployed site is 100x too large (e.g. $48000 instead of $480) because the build multiplies totals by 100 before writing the data file.
`npm start` always tries to bind to port 80, which fails with a permissions error on any machine that isn't running as root.
The order list only ever shows every other matching order; roughly half of them silently disappear.
The page's script can't find the order list container (id was renamed), so nothing ever renders even though the data loads fine.
